Spooky Eyeball Garland — Crochet Eyeballs on Jute Twine 👁️🎃

A spooky-cute vertical garland with 8 crochet eyeballs — blue, green, and brown irises with red veins — strung on jute twine for Halloween windows and doors.

I made this one on a dark October afternoon with my black wall behind me and pumpkins on my wooden table — just like in your photo with orange pumpkins, eucalyptus, autumn leaves, and golden fairy lights in the blurred background. A friend who loves spooky-cute Halloween asked for a garland that wasn't too scary — "Can you make eyeballs but cute?" So I sat with white, blue, green, brown, black, and red yarn, jute twine, and my tea going cold, and crocheted eyeballs while little plastic spiders sat on my table. By evening I had 8 eyeballs hanging vertically on twine on my black wall, and it made my whole room feel like Halloween.

Level Beginner — amigurumi balls + iris + veins — weekend make
Yarn Worsted — white 80g, blue 10g, green 10g, brown 10g, black 10g, red 5g for veins — 3.5mm hook — jute twine 5 feet — stitch markers, stuffing
Size Garland about 4 feet long vertical — eyeballs about 2.5" wide each — 8 eyeballs — spaced about 4.5" apart — iris colors blue, green, brown mixed

My yarn basket — white, blue, green, brown, black, red with jute twine

For this garland I used worsted weight yarn — soft white 80 grams for the eyeball whites, blue 10 grams, green 10 grams, brown 10 grams for irises, black 10 grams for pupils, and red 5 grams for veins. I use a 3.5mm hook so eyeballs are tight and round — not loose — about 2.5" wide each. I also had jute twine 5 feet long for vertical hanging — natural twine — just like in your photo with jute twine holding 8 eyeballs vertically on black wall, with orange pumpkins and eucalyptus at bottom.

My yarn basket — white, blue, green, brown, black, and red yarn balls with wooden hook, jute twine, scissors, and orange pumpkins on dark wooden table — beginning of spooky eyeball garland — real photo.

I use soft white with a little fuzz — not bright white — it looks like real eyeball white with slight texture and holds red veins well — and deep blue, green, brown for irises — just like in your photo with blue, green, brown eyes mixed.

How this eyeball garland is made — white balls + irises + red veins on twine

This garland is simple — you crochet 8 white balls — each about 2.5" wide — then crochet 8 irises — blue, green, brown mixed — 3 blue, 3 green, 2 brown — each iris about 1" wide with black pupil 0.4" in center — sew iris onto white ball — then embroider red veins with red yarn — about 8-10 little veins per eyeball radiating from iris outward — like in your photo with red veins on white eyeball. Then string 8 eyeballs vertically on jute twine 5 feet long, spaced about 4.5" apart — vertical hanging garland about 4 feet long — 8 eyeballs hanging down black wall — spooky-cute Halloween.

White eyeball balls — make 8 — 2.5" wide

EYEBALL BALLS — WHITE — 3.5MM — 2.5 INCH WIDE — MAKE 8
White eyeball balls — white, 3.5mm hook — make 8 — tight amigurumi balls:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc — 6
R2: inc 6 — 12
R3: [sc, inc]6 — 18
R4: [sc 2, inc]6 — 24
R5: [sc 3, inc]6 — 30 — 30 sts — about 2" wide
R6: [sc 4, inc]6 — 36 — 36 sts — widest about 2.5" wide — 36 sts
R7-12: sc 36 — 6 rounds straight — ball body about 1.5" tall — 36 each round — white eyeball ball — about 2.5" wide
R13: [sc 4, dec]6 — 30
R14: [sc 3, dec]6 — 24 — start stuffing — stuff firmly with polyfill — keep round shape
R15: [sc 2, dec]6 — 18
R16: [sc, dec]6 — 12 — stuff more — firm ball
R17: dec 6 — 6 — close with needle — weave tail inside — white ball about 2.5" wide, round — eyeball white
Make 8 white balls — each 2.5" wide — 36 sts widest — 6 rounds straight — stuff firmly — round eyeballs like in your photo with white background

Each white ball starts 6→36 — widest 2.5" wide at 36 sts — 6 rounds straight at 36 sts — body about 1.5" tall — then decrease 36→30→24→18→12→6 and close — stuff firmly with polyfill to keep round shape — white ball about 2.5" wide, round — make 8 white balls — like in your photo with white eyeball bases.

White eyeball ball in progress — white yarn ball open with hook and white yarn ball, scissors, pincushion, and notebook that says "crochet eyeball ball — round 8 / need to stuff add pupil keep 6 sts gap" — on wooden table with jack-o-lantern pumpkin, black candle, plastic spiders, bats, spider web — real photo — ball about 2.5" wide.

Irises — blue, green, brown with black pupils — make 8

IRISES — BLUE GREEN BROWN + BLACK PUPILS — 3.5MM — 1 INCH WIDE — MAKE 8
Irises — blue, green, brown, black, 3.5mm hook — make 8 irises:
Black pupil — black, 3.5mm — make 8:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc — 6 — pupil about 0.4" wide — 6 sts — black
Fasten off leave tail 6" — black pupil 0.4" wide — small black dot
Colored iris — blue, green, brown — make 8 — 3 blue, 3 green, 2 brown:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc with colored yarn — blue or green or brown — 6
R2: inc 6 — 12 — 12 sts — about 0.6" wide
R3: [sc, inc]6 — 18 — 18 sts — iris about 1" wide — 18 sts — colored iris 1" wide
Place black pupil in center of colored iris — sew with black tail — black pupil in middle of colored iris — iris 1" wide with 0.4" black pupil center — like in your photo with blue, green, brown irises and black pupils
Sew iris onto white ball:
Sew colored iris with black pupil onto white ball front center — about centered — use colored yarn tail — 6-8 stitches around edge — secure — iris 1" wide on white ball 2.5" wide — like in your photo where iris sits centered on white eyeball

Irises are small circles — black pupil 6 sc — 0.4" wide — colored iris 6→18 — 1" wide — place black pupil in center of colored iris and sew — then sew whole iris with pupil onto white ball front center — iris 1" wide on white ball 2.5" wide — make 8 irises — 3 blue, 3 green, 2 brown — like in your photo with blue, green, brown irises mixed vertically.

Three eyeballs with irises — blue, green, and brown irises with black pupils — each iris about 1" wide on white ball 2.5" wide — on wooden table with brown, blue, green yarn balls and hook — real photo — blue left, green middle, brown right.

Red veins — embroidered

RED VEINS — RED YARN EMBROIDERY — 8-10 VEINS PER EYEBALL
Red veins — red yarn, tapestry needle — embroidered on white ball:
Thread red yarn on tapestry needle — 18" long
Embroider red veins radiating from iris outward toward back of eyeball — about 8-10 veins per eyeball — each vein about 0.6-0.8" long — thin red lines — like blood veins — like in your photo with red veins on white eyeball
Veins pattern: 2 veins top, 2 bottom, 2 left, 2 right, 2 diagonal — total 8-10 veins — random — not symmetrical — more realistic — some veins fork into 2 at end — like real eye veins
Tie off and weave tail inside ball — red veins on white — spooky eyeball with veins — like in your photo with red veins on white balls

Red veins are embroidered with tapestry needle and red yarn — 18" long — about 8-10 veins per eyeball — each vein 0.6-0.8" long — radiating from iris outward toward back of ball — 2 top, 2 bottom, 2 left, 2 right, 2 diagonal — some veins fork into 2 at end like real eye veins — tie off and weave tail inside — like in your photo with red veins on white eyeballs with blue, green, brown irises.

Assembly — stringing 8 eyeballs vertically on jute twine

ASSEMBLY — 5 FEET JUTE TWINE — 4 FEET LONG VERTICAL GARLAND — 8 EYEBALLS
Assembly — string eyeballs vertically on jute twine 5 feet:
1. Cut jute twine 5 feet long — 60" — leaves 6" extra at top for hanging loop — garland will be about 4 feet long — 48" — with 8 eyeballs spaced about 4.5" apart
2. Eyeballs — 8 eyeballs — each 2.5" wide — 3 blue irises, 3 green irises, 2 brown irises — each with black pupil 0.4" and red veins 8-10 per ball
3. Spacing: 5 feet twine =60" total — minus 6" top hanging loop =54" usable — 8 eyeballs with 7 gaps — space eyeballs about 4.5" apart edge-to-edge (about 7" center-to-center) — this uses about 51.5" of your 54" usable twine (7 gaps ×4.5" =31.5" plus 8 eyeballs ×2.5" =20" =51.5"), leaving a little slack for tying knots — 4 feet long garland
4. Pattern along twine top to bottom: blue iris, green iris, brown iris, blue iris, green iris, brown iris, blue iris, green iris — alternating blue, green, brown — 3 blue, 3 green, 2 brown — like in your photo with blue top, green second, brown third, blue fourth, green fifth, brown sixth, blue seventh, green eighth — mixed colors
5. Attach each eyeball to twine — use white long tail — tie around twine with 2 knots at top of eyeball — or ch4 loop at top of white ball before closing and thread twine through loop — secure — eyeballs hang with iris facing forward
6. Make hanging loop at top — tie loop 3" diameter at top end of twine — for hanging on black wall or window — loop 3"
7. Bottom end — leave 2" tail or tie small knot — finish

I string 8 eyeballs vertically on jute twine 5 feet long — 60" total — with 6" extra at top for hanging loop, leaving 54" usable — 7 gaps between 8 eyeballs — space eyeballs about 4.5" apart edge-to-edge (about 7" center-to-center) — this uses about 51.5" of your 54" usable twine (7 gaps ×4.5" =31.5" plus 8 eyeballs ×2.5" =20" =51.5"), leaving a little slack for tying knots — so finished garland is about 4 feet long — 48" — pattern top to bottom: blue iris, green iris, brown iris, blue iris, green iris, brown iris, blue iris, green iris — alternating colors — 3 blue, 3 green, 2 brown — like in your photo where eyeballs hang vertically on black wall with blue top, green second, brown third, blue fourth, green fifth, brown sixth, blue seventh, green eighth — mixed blue, green, brown irises — each eyeball 2.5" wide with 1" iris and 0.4" black pupil and 8-10 red veins.

Assembly — eyeball garland being strung vertically on jute twine — hands tying twine with eyeballs with blue, green, brown irises — on dark wall — real photo — garland about 4 feet long in progress.

Finished — spooky eyeball garland on black wall

And here it is — my spooky-cute eyeball garland — about 4 feet long vertical — 5 feet jute twine with 3" hanging loop at top — with 8 eyeballs — each about 2.5" wide — white balls with 1" irises — 3 blue, 3 green, 2 brown — each with 0.4" black pupil in center and 8-10 red veins embroidered radiating from iris — spaced about 4.5" edge-to-edge, about 7" center-to-center — like in your photo with 8 eyeballs hanging vertically on black wall — blue, green, brown irises mixed — with orange pumpkins, eucalyptus, autumn leaves, and fairy lights at bottom.

Finished — spooky eyeball garland — 8 crochet eyeballs — 2.5" wide each — with blue, green, brown irises 1" wide and black pupils 0.4" and red veins — strung vertically on jute twine about 4 feet long — hanging on black wall with orange pumpkins, eucalyptus, autumn leaves, fairy lights — spooky-cute Halloween garland. 👁️🎃

When I hung it on my black wall next morning with pumpkins on my table and eucalyptus, my friend said, "Are those eyeballs? They're so cute and spooky!" I laughed and said, "I made them yesterday with white yarn and blue, green, brown for irises and red for veins." I hope you make yours on a cozy dark October afternoon too — maybe with pumpkins and eucalyptus nearby — and hang it on your black wall, window, or door for Halloween.

— Sara
